title: structured output: tighten CFG + regex backends, handle tokenizer edgecases in constrained decoding
author: Aisha Khan
description:
Motivation: Constrained decoding (CFG + regex backends) has surface-area bugs when tokenizers split control characters or produce unexpected token boundaries; this leads to streaming stalls, invalid structured outputs, and occasional downstream tool-calling failures. This PR tightens the two backends (CFG and regex) and normalizes tokenizer boundaries used by the decoders so that constraints are applied at the token level consistently across the OpenAI-compat layer and native streaming path.

What this PR does (summary):
- Fixes a tokenizer-edgecase where multi-codepoint unicode sequences and control tokens split across subword tokens causing regex/CFG matches to fail mid-stream. We add a normalization pass that compares decoded text spans with tokenizer token boundaries and prefers constraint application at safe token cut points.
- Improves the CFG backend to: 1) handle optional/nullable productions that previously allowed empty matches leading to infinite-loop-like behavior; 2) use a safer lookahead window for streaming so partial matches don't prematurely prune valid continuations.
- Harden regex backend: canonicalize regex anchors to token boundaries and add fallbacks when the tokenizer inserts whitespace tokens (common with CJK + punctuation).
- Add a compatibility shim in the OpenAI-compat layer so constrained decoding APIs behave the same whether a request came through the openai-style endpoint or the native /v1/generate streaming path. This reduces customer confusion and flakiness in third-party integrations.
- Add ~20 unit tests and 6 integration streaming regression tests that reproduce previously flaky cases (unicode combining chars, long lookahead CFG rules, regex with lookbehind interacting with token boundaries).

Implementation notes:
- New module: server/inference/decoding/tokenizer_boundary_utils.py (normalization helpers used by both backends). The module exposes a simple API: compute_safe_token_splits(text, token_offsets) and is intentionally small and deterministic.
- CFG backend changes in server/inference/decoding/cfg_backend.py: we changed the streamingmatcher to avoid accepting empty productions unless there is progress in the token stream, and we limited backtracking depth in streaming mode to avoid exponential cost on pathological grammars.
- Regex backend changes in server/inference/decoding/regex_backend.cc and regex_backend.py: we now translate regex to a token-aware NFA that respects token boundaries; we added a fast path for simple prefix/suffix regexes to avoid expensive lookaround on long sequences.
- OpenAI-compat changes: services/openai_compat/constrained_decoding_adapter.py ensures constraint metadata is serialized to the same canonical form used by the native API so the runtime picks the same backend path.
- Tests: tests/decoding/test_tokenizer_boundaries.py, tests/decoding/test_cfg_streaming_regressions.py, tests/integration/test_constrained_decoding_streaming.py.

Backwards-compatibility: No consumer-visible changes to existing constraint DSLs. Small behavioral change: previously-ambiguous grammars that relied on empty productions may now be rejected in streaming mode; such grammars were already non-deterministic and caused runtime stalls. We document this in release notes and added guidance on expressing optional branches.

Risk and rollout plan: CI includes a new integration suite that reproduces the incident from SUP-987. We will monitor streaming error-rate and tool-calling failure-rate for the next 48 hours after rollout. If any regression is observed, we can toggle to the previous (more permissive) CFG path via runtime flag 'decoding.cfg.strict_streaming=false' while debugging.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration streaming tests added
- [x] OpenAI-compat adapter updated
- [x] Docs/notes for grammar authors updated

release_notes: Structured output: tightened CFG and regex constrained-decoding backends to correctly handle tokenizer edgecases (unicode combining marks, CJK punctuation, and control tokens). Added tokenizer boundary normalization to reduce streaming stalls. OpenAI-compat layer now canonicalizes constraint serialization for consistent runtime behavior. This may cause stricter rejection of grammars that relied on empty productions in streaming mode; see docs/structured_output/constraints.md for recommended fixes.
